flawed_step: The claim that the parameters (n,k,lambda,mu) determine a strongly regular graph up to isomorphism, and in particular that every SRG(16,6,2,2) is K4 x K4.
counterexample: Shrikhande graph: vertices Z4xZ4, x~y iff x-y in S={±(1,0),±(0,1),±(1,1)}. It is 6-regular on 16 vertices. For each x, count s in S with x-s in S: x=(1,0) gives s=(0,3),(1,1), so lambda=2; x=(1,1) gives s=(1,0),(0,1), so lambda=2; x=(2,0) gives (1,0),(3,0), so mu=2; x=(2,2) gives (1,1),(3,3), so mu=2; x=(1,2) gives (0,1),(1,1), so mu=2; x=(1,3) gives (1,0),(0,3), so mu=2. All other vertices follow because coordinate swap and negation map S to itself. So it is SRG(16,6,2,2). The neighbourhood of 0 is the 6-cycle (1,0)-(1,1)-(0,1)-(3,0)-(3,3)-(0,3)-(1,0). In K4xK4 every vertex neighbourhood is two disjoint triangles, so the two graphs are not isomorphic.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The Shrikhande graph has parameters (16,6,2,2), checked directly as a Cayley graph on Z4xZ4. Its vertex neighbourhoods are 6-cycles, while those of the 4x4 rook's graph are two disjoint triangles, so the graphs are not isomorphic.
